question: Why do nurses regularly monitor a child's growth?

options.A: To calculate exact adult height and weight
options.B: To diagnose specific genetic disorders instantly
options.C: To catch health and nutritional problems early
options.D: To replace routine medical checkups entirely

explanation: You've got this! Growth monitoring helps us spot tiny changes or downward trends early on, long before a child gets seriously ill. It's a quick win for preventive care! [learn more](GNS227_U2_T005#GNS227_U2_T005_h1)

question: Why is plotting a child's measurements over time better than taking just a single measurement?

options.A: It is the only legal requirement for pediatric hospital admission
options.B: It reveals individual growth trends rather than just a one-time snapshot
options.C: It eliminates all possible errors made during the weighing process
options.D: It removes the need to use standard growth charts

explanation: Think of it like a movie versus a single photograph. One measurement only shows you right now, but tracking over time shows the real direction and speed of the child's development. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T005#GNS227_U2_T005_h1)

question: Which gland is responsible for releasing the main growth hormone that helps children grow taller?
explanation: Great recall! The anterior pituitary gland pumps out growth hormone, which teams up with other hormones to stretch those bones and build tissues during childhood. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T005#GNS227_U2_T005_h2)

question: At what stage of life is a child's physical growth speed (velocity) at its absolute highest?
explanation: Babies grow faster than at any other time in their lives! That rapid change is why infants need so much energy and good nutrition packed into their tiny bodies. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T005#GNS227_U2_T005_h2)

question: For how long is exclusive breastfeeding recommended for a healthy baby?
explanation: Spot on! Exclusive breastfeeding for the first six months gives babies the absolute best nutrition and shields them against common childhood sicknesses. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T005#GNS227_U2_T005_h3)

question: A healthy toddler suddenly starts eating less food than before. What is the most likely reason for this?

options.A: Growth velocity naturally slows down after infancy, reducing food demand
options.B: The child is entering a severe phase of permanent nutritional failure
options.C: Breast milk or formula is no longer needed in any form
options.D: The child has developed an irreversible eating disorder

explanation: Don't panic if a toddler's appetite dips! Because growth slows down after year one, they simply don't need as many calories per kilogram. It's completely normal. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T005#GNS227_U2_T005_h3)

question: What equipment do you need to measure the height (length) of a child who is under two years old?
explanation: Since under-twos won't stand straight and still for a stadiometer, we lay them flat and use a dedicated infant length board to get an accurate reading. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T005#GNS227_U2_T005_h4)

question: Why must a nurse use a non-stretchable tape when measuring head and arm circumferences?

options.A: To prevent measurement errors caused by material stretching over time
options.B: To ensure the tape can be washed easily with boiling water
options.C: To comply with weight limits on heavy clinical scales
options.D: To make the equipment safe for the child to play with

explanation: Materials stretch with use! If your tape stretches, your next readings will be off, messing up the child's growth tracking records. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T005#GNS227_U2_T005_h4)

question: What does a low height-for-age measurement mainly tell us about a young child?
explanation: Height-for-age looks at the long picture. If it's low, it usually points to stunting caused by long-term poor nutrition or repeated illnesses over time. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T005#GNS227_U2_T005_h5)

question: A child's weight-for-length falls way below the minus two Z-score on the growth chart. What does this mean?
explanation: You're doing great! Weight-for-length compares mass to height. A very low score means the child has recently lost weight and is too thin for their height—a sign of wasting. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T005#GNS227_U2_T005_h5)

question: Which clinical sign helps you tell kwashiorkor apart from marasmus?

options.B: Extreme loss of all body fat

explanation: Remember: Kwashiorkor is tied to severe protein lack, which leads to fluid retention (pitting edema), especially making the legs and face look swollen. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T005#GNS227_U2_T005_h6)

question: What is the very first sign a nurse looks for on a growth chart to spot growth faltering?

options.A: A stable horizontal line that matches the birth weight
options.B: A sudden spike in height above the ninety-fifth percentile
options.C: A flattening or downward crossing of weight percentiles
options.D: An abrupt increase in head circumference beyond normal limits

explanation: Growth faltering happens quietly at first—the child stops gaining weight along their usual curve, causing the line to flatten or dip across the percentile tracks. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T005#GNS227_U2_T005_h6)

question: What is a crucial first step when caring for a malnourished child who also has an acute infection?

options.A: Treat the underlying infection alongside nutritional support
options.B: Restrict all oral fluids to prevent electrolyte imbalances
options.C: Discharge the child immediately for home management
options.D: Wait until the child regains full weight before giving medicines

explanation: Infections and malnutrition make a dangerous pair because sickness steals appetite and burns energy. Treating the infection right away is a life-saving priority! [learn more](GNS227_U2_T005#GNS227_U2_T005_h7)

question: A mother cannot afford the expensive imported supplements recommended for her underweight toddler. As her nurse, what should you do?

options.A: Tell her that nutrition counseling is no longer necessary if she cannot afford items
options.B: Help the mother adapt affordable, locally available foods to enrich the child's diet
options.C: Advise her to stop feeding the child solid foods until financial aid arrives
options.D: Insist that she buy the expensive supplements regardless of her financial situation

explanation: Real nursing meets people where they are. Great health education uses accessible, local market foods to make nutritious meals practical for every family. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T005#GNS227_U2_T005_h7)
